On Jun 1, 2009, at 13:36 , Anya Okhmatovskaia wrote:

> Hi,
>

> no such class in the new client package, so I wonder what I should  
> use instead? (I am trying to migrate my code to using the new client)

RBool wrapper is no longer needed. You can use REXPLogical directly  
instead. It accepts either boolean arrays (this doesn't allow NAa) or  
byte arrays with the values REXPLogical.TRUE, REXPLogical.FALSE or  
REXPLogical.NA. When retrieved you can either use asBytes() or one of  
isTRUE(), isFALSE(), isNA().

see
http://rforge.net/Rserve/doc/

The latest Rserve now also includes support for assignment of logical  
vectors (you'll need the latest Rserve from rforge.net and the  
contained client for that).

Cheers,
Simon

messages.subject: possible severe bug: JGR 1.6.5 mixes up file names and can destroy script files (on Ubuntu 9.04)
messages.subject_clean: possible severe bug: JGR 1.6.5 mixes up file names and can destroy script files (on Ubuntu 9.04)
messages.body_plain:
-----BEGIN PGP SIGNED MESSAGE-----
Hash: SHA1

Hi,

JGR seems to mix up names of files opened in Editor windows on Ubuntu
9.04. There is some danger that existing scripts are overwritten and
destroyed by JGR.

To reproduce this, generate two tiny files

/---file: t1.r---\
| # one          |
\--- file end ---/


/---file: t2.r---\
| # two          |
\--- file end ---/

Scenario I:

1. Within JGR Console use the new "Open"-icon and open file t1.r. A new
Editor window will open. "# one" is displayed. (Note: There is no
filename in the titlebar of this window.)

2. Within this new Editor window (seems to be important to reproduce
behaviour) press the "Open"-icon and open t2.r. A new Editor window
opens with the file name in the titlebar, "# two" is displayed.

3. Switch to the Editor window where file t1.r is opened ("# one" in the
editor field). Press "Save"-Icon. The _wrong_ (!) file name t2.r appears
(with path) in the titlebar of this first editor window.

4. Check file t2.r with an other editor (here: gedit). File t2.r
consists now only of "# one", which means that file t2.r was overwritten
(!) by a editor window which should only control file t1.r.

Scenario II:

1. Open t1.r. Only on pressing "Save"-Icon the file name appears in the
title bar.

2. Within this editor window (seems to be important to reproduce
behaviour) press the "Open"-icon and open t2.r. No (!) new window opens.
The file contens ("# two") of the selected file (t2.r) is displayed
under the name t1.r (in the title bar).

3. Press "Save": The file name in the titlebar changes back to t2.r.
Nothing severe happend, but it would be a good idea to display always
the right file names in the title bar.

Here on a Ubuntu 9.04 computer I can always reproduce this behaviour.
Please let me know if you need additional informations to solve this.

Best regards

Knut Wenzig

Yes, in the current tests data sizes of 1mio - 10mio data points pose

Possibly, but it's a lesser priority now with the fast performance.

I expect to release the new iPlots soon after useR/DSC, but even if  
that should become a longer delay, the sources and binary packages  
will be publicly available from RForge.net before the conferences.

Cheers,
Simon

messages.subject: .jrcall, reflection problem ?
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am trying to write a with.jobjRef in order to run several methods 
"with" the same object using reflection tricks similar to what the $ 
method does. See 
http://romainfrancois.blog.free.fr/index.php?post/2009/06/17/with-semantics-for-java-objects-in-rJava

It kind of works, but there are some issues with .jrcall I guess:

 > f <- .jnew( "javax/swing/JFrame" )
 > lab <- .jnew( "javax/swing/JLabel", "Hello" )
 > f$add( lab )
Error in .jrcall(x, name, ...) :
  Cannot find Java method `add' matching the supplied parameters.

where this works:

 > .jcall( f, "Ljava/awt/Component;", "add", .jcast( lab , 
"java/awt/Component") )

but this does not :

 > f$add( .jcast( lab, "java/awt/Component")  )
Error in .jrcall(x, name, ...) :
  Cannot find Java method `add' matching the supplied parameters.

My questions are:
- why do we have to .jcast in the .jcall call
- is it possible to call f$add( lab )

The method I am actually trying to call is this:
public java.awt.Component java.awt.Container.add(java.awt.Component)

So I guess there are two issues:
- f is a JFrame, not "exactly" a Component
- lab is a JLabel, not "exactly" a Component

I think I could write a little java utility that would look for 
candidate methods in the super classes and implemented interfaces of "f" 
and try to match these against the arguments. Would this be useful to 
others ? If so, where should this be ?

Romain

as java.awt.Component.


> where this works:
>
>> .jcall( f, "Ljava/awt/Component;", "add", .jcast( lab , "java/awt/ 
>> Component") )
>

(as expected)


> but this does not :
>
>> f$add( .jcast( lab, "java/awt/Component")  )
> Error in .jrcall(x, name, ...) :
>  Cannot find Java method `add' matching the supplied parameters.
>

The reflection ignores any casting you do, therefore the .jcast has no  
effect. Instead the reflection calls getClass() on the object which  
here returns javax.swing.JLabel.


> My questions are:
> - why do we have to .jcast in the .jcall call

Because Java requires exact match of argument types for methods (as  
well as the return type). In compiled Java code the compiler does that  
lookup for you but .jcall is the direct interface to the JVM so all  
parameters must match.


> - is it possible to call f$add( lab )
>

This one is actually startling - Java's reflection denies that `f' can  
be used as an argument to "add". You can in fact check that directly:

 > fc=.jcall(f,"Ljava/lang/Class;","getClass")
 > lc=.jcall(lab,"Ljava/lang/Class;","getClass")
 > (m=.jcall(fc,"Ljava/lang/reflect/ 
Method;","getMethod","add",.jarray(lc,"java/lang/Class")))
NULL

but if you force the class it works:

 > lc=.jcall("java/lang/Class","Ljava/lang/ 
Class;","forName","java.awt.Component")
 > (m=.jcall(fc,"Ljava/lang/reflect/ 
Method;","getMethod","add",.jarray(lc,"java/lang/Class")))
[1] "Java-Object{public java.awt.Component  
java.awt.Container.add(java.awt.Component)}"

One way out here would be to use the cast class in the reflection so  
you could actually use f$add(.jcast(...)).


> The method I am actually trying to call is this:
> public java.awt.Component java.awt.Container.add(java.awt.Component)
>
> So I guess there are two issues:
> - f is a JFrame, not "exactly" a Component

That is not really relevant since the method is called on that  
objects, so we're safe there.


> - lab is a JLabel, not "exactly" a Component
>

Yes - at least for .jcall. For the reflection is should actually, work  
- I'm not sure why it doesn't ...


> I think I could write a little java utility that would look for  
> candidate methods in the super classes and implemented interfaces of  
> "f" and try to match these against the arguments. Would this be  
> useful to others ? If so, where should this be ?
>


Exhaustive search would be really slow, but I suppose it could be an  
useful fallback. You can get a list of all methods using  
Class.getMethods(), but the actually matching may be a bit tricky --  
but very useful if it can make it to the .jrcall [that's where the  
reflection is done, but I should really rewrite it since it precedes  
support for arrays in rJava...].

Cheers,
Simon

JavaGD doesn't require rJava - it works even without it, that's why it  
doesn't "depend" on it. It uses its own JNI code. The messages you see  
are benign - JavaGD is trying various ways to load the JavaGD class.  
(I'm not sure why those messages appear since those exceptions should

otherwise JavaGD initializes the JVM before rJava, so rJava cannot do  
much of its magic. It will still work, but you can get unpleasant  
issues with the class loader depending on which class loader another  
class etc.

You don't need to create strings explicitly via .jnew. Other than that  
plus using shorthand for integers it's no different from this

tz <- .jcall("java/util/TimeZone", "Ljava/util/TimeZone;",  
"getTimeZone", "GMT")

.. but whether it's a better way that's not well-defined ;)

In general when something doesn't work consult a) documentation for  
the classes you're using and b) use .jmethods to see what are the  
required types.

To answer your original question

calendar.set(Calendar.DAY_OF_MONTH, 1);

will turn into

.jcall(calendar,,"set", .jfield(calendar,"I","DAY_OF_MONTH"), 1L)

If you are using this interactively, you can also write it as:

calendar$set(calendar$DAY_OF_MONTH, 1L)

but for this last trick you'll need the latest rJava 0.6-4 from http://rforge.net/rJava/

Simon

messages.subject: various suggestions for JGR
messages.body_plain:
Dear JGR developers,

First, thank you for the very helpful programme you develop.
I have used JGR in a recent project and I have assembled a list of
suggestions, some important and most minor, which could however
improve the experience of JGR users. This is also in part a reply to
yesterday's post by Ian Fellows [1].
[1] http://markmail.org/message/bu2pcwwfq6oc332w

One important detail is that I'm using JGR on an Xfce-desktoped Gentoo
Linux. Also, please excuse the length of the e-mail.


Major issues:
- JGR will crash whenever the "cancel" button is pressed. This happens
also on Mac, and can be a painful experience for unaware users. To
reproduce run any time consuming code, say `for(i in
1:10000){rnorm(10000)}', and hit "cancel" before the code finishes.
- pressing the up/down arrows in the console input can result in data
loss; take the simple three-liner that was just typed in:
for(i in 1:10000){
    rnorm(10000)
}

Whenever I move the cursor to "f" or "}", subsequepressing up/down
will result in losing everything that was typed. I could press it by
inattention, or wanting to select some code with <shift>+up/down, or
whatever. The result is, unfortunately, that the code written is lost.
Now this is fine for this three-liner, but when it happens a couple of
times in an hour for 7-10 lines of code that you take 10-12 min to
produce, you start paying unnecessarily much attention to when and how
you use the arrow keys. I would see two possible solutions to this: 1.
Make JGR behave as UNIX consoles do; that is, every time a history (or
new) element is edited, the edit is recorded and even if the user does
<up> followed by <down> the edited element is still there, or 2. make,
say, <ctrl>+arrows the bindings for accessing history elements instead
of simply <arrows>.
- there are issues if JGR is instructed to load Rcmdr at start-up;
previous versions caused Rcmdr to hang, while latest version makes
Rcmdr very slow (when accessing any menu, for example). There are no
such issues if Rcmdr is started from JGR's console via require(Rcmdr).


Editor issues:
- when nothing is selected, upon <ctrl>+r JGR could execute the line
where the cursor is located. I'm not entirely sure whether this is a
good idea, but I often come across one-liners in my code and it feels
strange to always select the entire line in order to execute it.
- when opening an .R script, the "modified" tag (bottom-right hand
side) will be displayed whenever I move the cursor or click with the
mouse anywhere on the code. This can be disconcerting since one never
knows when one truly made an edit (or a typo) in the document. I
believe the "modified" tag (and the subsequent "save file?" dialogue)
would be much more helpful if it appeared only when "genuine"
modifications were made to the file.
- add a "reload file from disk" menu item (with a confirmation
dialogue); this can be most helpful when user wants to do the heavy
editing in her preferred text editor, and then quickly reopen the file
in JGR to run the code. A nice addition to this would be to
automatically pop up a dialogue proposing to "reload file from disk"
whenever the time-stamp of the disk file is newer than the time-stamp
of the file that was initially opened (or last saved with JGR); this
would suggest that the  file was edited somewhere else, and that it
might make sense to reload it from disk. In Geany, the message is as
follows: "The file 'untitled3' on the disk is more recent than the
current buffer. Do you want to reload it?"
- make comment out/uncomment items work; here i never managed to
add/rem "#" in front of the current line with these menu items


Console issues:
- make possible to execute the text selected in the output window with
a ctrl+r command, similar to how code can be executed in Help. Of
course one can quickly find the previously issued command in history
and edit it, or select the desired text, drag-and-drop it and <enter>,
but it would often be so much easier to simply select parts of
previously issued commands and <ctrl>+r them.
- make behaviour of <tab> completion similar to that in the default R
terminal; example: currently in JGR typing `req' and hitting <tab>
would pop up a completion dialogue with items `require' and
`requireMethods', while in the R terminal after hitting <tab> the
command name will immediately get auto-completed until the full string
that is shared by all possible functions, `require', and then the two
available functions are suggested: `require' and `requireMethods'. I
believe that it would make sense for JGR also immediately
auto-complete until `require' and display the available options; thus
if user is happy with the auto-completion, she can immediately
continue with the `('  rest of her command (and an <enter> is
avoided).
- tab completion fails in various circumstances:
   - issue `data(cars); RegModel.1 <- lm(speed~dist, data=cars)'; now
try `summary(RegModel.1)$<tab>' and the following error message will
pop out: "Error in get(sub("\\$", "", x)) : invalid first argument"; I
would expect it to fail silently, since the object doesn't exist yet.
   - similar issue with objects starting with a `.' (dot);
`.RegModel.1 <- lm(speed~dist, data=cars)' and `.RegModel.1$<tab>'
will generate "Error in get(sub("\\$", "", x)) : variable
"\.RegModel\.1" was not found". The error seems to affect any object
containing a dot, such as `RegModel.1'.
   - I ran into some other random failures of $<tab> completion of
objects, but didn't keep trace of all of them


Help system issues:
- JGR fails to load vignettes. It will load them as text files in the
help system (output that is unreadable), but not load them in a pdf
viewer. It might be useful to allow the user to "copy the address" via
a context-menu item.
- The default Help options can yield unexpected results. Search `acf'
and you would unexpectedly fall on `acf {dse1}'; I would have expected
`acf {stats}', or a list containing the latter (the result when "exact
match" is unchecked, and "object names" is checked). Similar surprises
will await when looking for `Commander' (default result is `Commander
{QCAGUI}'), or others. It's not always so; searching for `lm' will
expectedly find `lm {stats}'. However I feel that default Help
behaviour might be improved.
- I cannot understand whether unchecking "help agent" is functioning
correctly. When unchecked, I would expect JGR to no longer catch help
page requests, such as ?princomp or help(package=sandwich), and the
result to be displayed in a way similar to how it is in the R
terminal. Also, `help(package=sandwich)' always fails in JGR ("No
matches for "package=sandwich" have been found!"), although I often
want to see the main help page of a package, which lists the author,
dependencies, a short summary, etc.; I couldn't find a way to display
such information in JGR.


Windows issues:
- make JGR remember the last window position and size; JGR always
starts with a main window that vertically slightly exceeds the
available desktop space, and horizontally exceeds half of the screen
- the above should also apply to editor windows; each time I open a
file (either new or existing) the editor window vertically exceeds the
entire screen. Luckily on Xfce I can easily (via a shortcut)
vertically maximise the editor window bringing it back on screen and
then resize as I wish. When using JGR on Fluxbox this, however, has
been quite disconcerting
- the same issue touches the find dialogue in the editor or help. It
always starts much to the right of the concerned window, and since the
help/editor is most of the time on the right, the find dialogue always
displays over 80% off-screen. Displaying the dialogue in the middle of
the concerned window would probably suit most users.
- similar issues arise when displaying objects by double-clicking them
in the object browser; they would often be either slightly or >50%
off-screen.
I am not sure whether the issues above are more JGR or Xfce's window
manager related.


Well, this was a long e-mail. I would be happy if someone from the
devel team had the patience to read it through. Also, please let me
know if you prefer that I file bug reports for specific issues of
interest.
Best regards,
Liviu

Main thing for any power user of an interactive programing  language are  
shortkeys:
  - Basic navigation keys  
(http://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_node/emacs/Moving-Point.html#
Moving-Point).  
Mouse is a trap. With proper short keys for code navigation  
(words,sentences,paragraphs, code chunks (sexps)) one becomes k-folds more  
efficient.

  - Sending code from editor in different ways (line, paragraph, function,  
selection). And potentially combination of those - say if text is  
selected, then region is executed if not, one line is sent to console and  
the cursor is moved to the next one.

  - All short keys are better be customizable, like in emacs or  lyx - one  
startup file with simple description of associated commands.

> There are a couple of newer features
> which have made it suit my needs better. We recently added preference  
> items
> to change the output and command colors, as well as the editor syntax
> coloring which can now psuedo-emulate the coloring of emacs, xcode,  
> ecplise,
> vim, and visual studio. Auto-tabbing was also added, though it is  
> simplistic
> as of yet. What features would you like to see in a console?
>

JGR still lacks "previous matching input" behavior - only those lines are  
recalled that match starting string in command window.

Navigation by keys through previous output can be useful. Execution of  
previous lines from output window are of great help(probably quite a task  
for JGR since that window is not editable).

Other things like code folding and outlining in editor, point sensitive  
help are of not that much importance but could improve efficiency as well.

> Regarding other platforms... Right now the code is tied into JGR, but it
> wouldn't be too hard to port it to a different platform. JGR has the
> advantage that it is fully Java based, which make the development of  
> Deducer
> easier. I don't really know much about ess or sciviews, but in order to  
> be
> used, a platform would need 1. access to rJava 2. a way to enter commands
> into the terminal from java 3. a way to add menu items and hook them up  
> to
> java methods. For the time being I'm pretty committed to using JGR, when
> Deducer is more mature I'll think about supporting others.
>
Deducer is a great fit, no doubt about that. R lack of internal  
spreadsheet is sometimes annoying. In my view, if Deducer could replace  
R's edit() command then not only JGR users but the whole community would  
benefit enormously. Just to find a way to link it to R process. I don't  
know much about rJava or how ESS internals work but taking into  
consideration versatility of emacs that probably won't be a problem. For  
instance Rcmder works reasonably well with ESS and all other guis; Why not  
a stand alone Deducer?

Thanks again for sharing the application. A very useful start indeed.

Best,
Vitalie.

will generate "Error in get(sub("\\$", "", x)) : variable
"\.RegModel\.1" was not found". The error seems to affect any object
containing a dot, such as `RegModel.1'.
   - I ran into some other random failures of $<tab> completion of
objects, but didn't keep trace of all of them


Help system issues:
- JGR fails to load vignettes. It will load them as text files in the
help system (output that is unreadable), but not load them in a pdf
viewer. It might be useful to allow the user to "copy the address" via
a context-menu item.
- The default Help options can yield unexpected results. Search `acf'
and you would unexpectedly fall on `acf {dse1}'; I would have expected
`acf {stats}', or a list containing the latter (the result when "exact
match" is unchecked, and "object names" is checked). Similar surprises
will await when looking for `Commander' (default result is `Commander
{QCAGUI}'), or others. It's not always so; searching for `lm' will
expectedly find `lm {stats}'. However I feel that default Help
behaviour might be improved.
- I cannot understand whether unchecking "help agent" is functioning
correctly. When unchecked, I would expect JGR to no longer catch help
page requests, such as ?princomp or help(package=sandwich), and the
result to be displayed in a way similar to how it is in the R
terminal. Also, `help(package=sandwich)' always fails in JGR ("No
matches for "package=sandwich" have been found!"), although I often
want to see the main help page of a package, which lists the author,
dependencies, a short summary, etc.; I couldn't find a way to display
such information in JGR.


Windows issues:
- make JGR remember the last window position and size; JGR always
starts with a main window that vertically slightly exceeds the
available desktop space, and horizontally exceeds half of the screen
- the above should also apply to editor windows; each time I open a
file (either new or existing) the editor window vertically exceeds the
entire screen. Luckily on Xfce I can easily (via a shortcut)
vertically maximise the editor window bringing it back on screen and
then resize as I wish. When using JGR on Fluxbox this, however, has
been quite disconcerting
- the same issue touches the find dialogue in the editor or help. It
always starts much to the right of the concerned window, and since the
help/editor is most of the time on the right, the find dialogue always
displays over 80% off-screen. Displaying the dialogue in the middle of
the concerned window would probably suit most users.
- similar issues arise when displaying objects by double-clicking them
in the object browser; they would often be either slightly or >50%
off-screen.
I am not sure whether the issues above are more JGR or Xfce's window
manager related.


Well, this was a long e-mail. I would be happy if someone from the
devel team had the patience to read it through. Also, please let me
know if you prefer that I file bug reports for specific issues of
interest.
Best regards,
Liviu

In fact I was thinking of this after your last contributions ;). There  
are some practical issues (it's easier to allow prefixes instead of  
enumerating packages for classes included), but it's something that  
can be done. However, in order to do this properly, it's not quite  
trivial, because we'd need to hash the names after lookup etc. For the  
reflection API I have no objection at all, because the user expects a  
performance hit, but for the low-level API it's not that clear

environment (or Java object) recursively and then on the search path  
such that packages can create one for their own namespace ... but I'm  
not sure how to make this really intuitive ... Probably along the  
lines what S4 does in packages ...

Cheers,
Simon

I have been using Mondrian for many months and have been frustrated that 
when using selections I could augment my current selection using the 
SHIFT-ALT key combination.  The ALT key works as it should to show the 
cursor coordinates in scatterplots and the SHIFT key works as it should 
as an XOR modifier when modifiying a selection.  But SHIFT-ALT does 
nothing and no mouse action report is given in the terminal window when 
I use it.  I have tried this with the openjdk that comes with Fedora 10 
and I have installed the latest Sun Java jre (1.6.0 rev 14), but it 
makes no difference.  I am using a Dell XPS 410, but I have had the same 
experience on my other computers running Fedora 10.

When I was struggling with this again today, I was once again trying 
some different key combinations and I discovered that the intended 
behavior of SHIFT-ALT does work if I also hold down the "Windows" key on 
my keyboard!  What I call the "Windows" key is the key with the Windows 
logo in the lower left part of my Dell keyboard between the CTRL and ALT 
keys.  So if I hold down all three keys, SHIFT-Windows-ALT and use the 
left mouse button I can modify selections with AND or OR (whichever I 
have chosen in the Mondrian Options menu).

I have no idea why this works, but I am glad to gain this functionality 
and I want to report it in case it helps others.

messages.body_plain:
Hello,

would it make sense in the REngine API to have a convenience like this :

public REXP call( String function, REXP... arguments ) ;

so that we can do something like this:

REXP n = new REXPInteger( 10 );
REXP mean = new REXPDouble( 2.0 ) ;
r.call( "rnorm", n, mean ) ;

which would mimic this R call :

rnorm( n, mean )

Obvisouly this example is not so useful, but i think having this 
functionality might prevent the idiom of assigning variables in the R 
global environment, and making the call.

It might get tricky when we also want to mimic this :

rnorm( n, sd = 2.0 )

i.e using named arguments, but it would not be too hard to encapsulate 
the name of the argument and the REXP in an Object.

Another issue is that we might want the method to have this signature:

public REXP call( String function, Object... arguments ) ;

and bring objects that are not REXP as java object references in the R 
side.

I would be happy to try to work on a patch if this is judged a useful 
feature.

Romain

> - that above is just a special case that maps into call(new

Ok. If we can agree on the interface, I'll take a shot.

How about this one:

REXP call( REXP function, REXP where, boolean resolve, REXP... arguments)

and this one

REXP call( REXP function, REXP... arguments)
as a shortcut to REXP( function, globalenv, true, arguments)
